sentences.text:
=
 Appearance:
 Dinesh M Desai(9086) for the Applicant(s) No. 1
 Mr Satish A Pandya(556) for the Applicant(s) No. 1
 Mr.Himanshu Patel, App for the Respondent(s) No. 1
 ==========================================================
 Coram:Honourable Mr. Justice M. R. Mengdey
 Date : 07/11/2025
Oral Order

1. This application is filed under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita for regular bail in connection with F.I.R. No.52 of 2019 registered with Sabarmati Police Station, District Ahmedabad for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 120(B), 170 and 114 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

2. Learned advocate for the applicant has submitted that the prosecution has cited 185 witnesses in the Charge-sheet and having regard to the number of witnesses cited by the prosecution, there is no possibility of trial getting over in near future.

He has further submitted that the applicant has been arrested in connection of the present offence in the year 2020 and though, the applicant had absconded for some time, he has undergone incarceration for long time and prolonged incarceration would amount to pretrial conviction.

He has therefore submitted that considering the nature of offence and NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/17860/2025 ORDER DATED: 07/11/2025 undefined role attributed to the applicant, the applicant may be enlarged on regular bail by imposing suitable conditions.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned APP appearing for the respondent State has vehemently submitted that after being released on temporary bail in the year 2021, the applicant had absconded for 1302 days.

He has further submitted that the allegations against the applicant, are serious in nature and looking to the facts as well as the allegations made against the applicant, no discretion should be exercised.
4.
Heard learned advocates for the respective parties and perused the documents produced on record.
This Court vide order dated 04.09.2025 had asked the learned trial Court to submit its report as regards the current status of trial.
Accordingly, the learned trial Court has submitted its Report dated 16.09.2025 which indicates that the applicant was ordered to be enlarged on temporary bail till 31.03.2021.
However, thereafter, the applicant had not surrendered before the concerned jail authority on 31.03.2021 and instead had absconded.
The total period of abscondance of the applicant is about 1302 days which is almost 4 years which indicates that the applicant had misused liberty granted to him by the concerned Court.
5. Considering the aforesaid facts, this Court is not inclined to exercise its judicial discretion in favour of the applicant.
The application is dismissed.

(M. R. MENGDEY,J) NABILA Amrutbhai @ Amratbhai Maganbhai Desai vs State Of Gujarat on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192779459/
